title: Basic test
description: Create a static method suma that receives two integers and returns their sum. Then write manual tests that verify suma(2, 3) returns 5, suma(0, 0) returns 0, and suma(-1, 1) returns 0. Use a manual comparison that prints PASS or FAIL for each case.
hints: The suma method simply returns a + b
For each test, compare the expected result with the actual one using if-else
If they are equal print 'PASS: suma(2, 3) = 5', otherwise 'FAIL: expected 5, got X'
solutionExplanation: The suma method is trivial and returns a + b. The tests are written manually, comparing the expected result with the one obtained using if-else statements. Each test prints PASS if the result is correct, or FAIL with the expected and obtained values if it is not. This is the basic testing pattern: arrange (prepare data), act (execute), assert (verify the result).
expectedOutput:
PASS: suma(2, 3) = 5
PASS: suma(0, 0) = 0
PASS: suma(-1, 1) = 0

title: Calculator tests
description: Create a Calculadora class with methods for addition, subtraction, multiplication and division. Then write tests for each method: at least 2 tests per operation (normal case and case with negatives or zero). For division, include a test that verifies it throws ArithmeticException when dividing by zero.
hints: For division, check whether b is 0 before dividing and throw ArithmeticException
To test that an exception is thrown, use try-catch and verify that the catch block runs
Use a counter for passed and failed tests to show a summary at the end
solutionExplanation: The Calculadora class implements the four basic operations, with validation of division by zero. The tests cover two cases per operation: a normal case and one with negative values. The exception test verifies that division by zero throws ArithmeticException using try-catch: if the exception is not thrown, the test fails. Finally, a summary with the count of passed and failed tests is shown.

PASS: division(10,2) = 5

title: Complete tests
description: Create a CalculadoraCientifica class with methods: suma, resta, multiplicacion, division, potencia (use Math.pow), and raizCuadrada (use Math.sqrt). Write complete tests covering: normal cases, edge cases (zero, one), negatives for square root, and division by zero. Use a final report with total, passed and failed.
hints: Use double for all methods to support decimals
To compare doubles use an epsilon: Math.abs(obtenido - esperado) < epsilon
Include tests with 0, 1, and negative numbers as edge cases
The final report must show the total tests executed, how many passed and how many failed
solutionExplanation: The CalculadoraCientifica implements six operations including power (Math.pow) and square root (Math.sqrt). 18 tests are written covering: (1) normal cases for each operation, (2) edge cases such as zero, one, and negatives, (3) exception tests for division by zero and square root of negatives. To compare doubles, an epsilon is used to avoid floating-point precision issues. The final report shows complete execution statistics. This pattern is the foundation of professional testing in Java with frameworks like JUnit.
